summary: R285 converts the one-shot R284 object materializer into a persistent NativeBackend-owned programmable shader ownership boundary. Exact R284/R242 receipts are retained and reused per programmable pair, the current R242 object receipt is fed directly into R275 semantic receipt composition, and NativeBackend initialization/shutdown ties the cache to its native D3D11 device generation. No shader/context binding, shaderTranslationExact promotion, NativeDrawPath activation or Draw/DrawIndexed dispatch is enabled.
evidence: native_backend.hpp adds NativeProgrammableShaderBackendSemanticHandoffEvidence and NativeProgrammableShaderBackendOwnership with persistent per-cacheKey R284 receipt storage.

native_backend.cpp validates an existing R284 receipt before reuse, obtains the current R242 translation-object readiness from the same native device/cache/slot, and composes/validates the R275 translated-semantic receipt.
The R285 entrypoint accepts no ID3D11DeviceContext and explicitly keeps objectBindingAuthorized, nativeDrawPathActivationAllowed and drawDispatchAuthorized false.
NativeBackend::initialize initializes the R285 owner on device_.Get(); NativeBackend::shutdown invalidates R285 ownership before releasing the D3D11 device.

WARP hosted regression proves the first exact R284->R242->R275 handoff, idempotent reuse for a repeated pair without shader recreation, unbound immediate-context VS/PS state, stale R274 mapping rejection, and device-generation invalidation.
tools/verify_dx11_source_graph.py guards the R285 owner, R275 feed, NativeBackend lifetime integration and no-binding/no-draw boundary.
